1171:
Where approval is sought for a plat which depicts the subdivision of a tract of land into not more than four lots or tracts of land, including the remaining portion of the original tract which shall be treated as one of the four lots, the following conditions must be met:
(1) The size and shape of each lot resulting from the subdivision must meet the minimum standards set forth in chapter 90 of this Code for the zoning district in which the land being subdivided is located, except that if the parent tract does not have 150 feet of public road frontage the subdivision may be approved if it provides access to the newly formed lots as described in subsection (2) below.
(2) Ingress and egress to each lot resulting from the subdivision is provided by an access road at least 30 feet in width fronting on a public road of not less than 30 feet in width, with a curb cut for the access road of not less than 18 feet in width. Such access road shall run back to some or all four of the lots in the subdivision by frontage on a private road of not less than 30 feet in width with the owners of the lots owning either fee simple title to, or a permanent easement over, a strip or strips of land not less than 30 feet in width which permanent easement or fee simple strip may be exclusive to one or more of the lots or non-exclusive for use by all of the lots; provided that all of the lots must have the required ingress and egress. Such fee simple title or permanent easement shall not serve land not included in the subdivision as shown on the plat. Under no circumstances shall there be more than two access roads serving the lots in the subdivision. The topography of such 30-foot wide strip or strips of land must be suitable for the construction and maintenance of an access road to the lots being served, and it must not be burdened with improvements, easements or other encumbrances that would interfere with its use as a right-of-way for an access road. Any access road serving the lots must consist of dirt, gravel or a higher grade paving surface at least 18 feet in width. The access road can be maintained on a surface of dirt except at the point where the access road intersects the public road where the paving of the access road must consist at least of gravel from the edge of the paved county road to the right-of-way line of the county road in order to protect the paving of the county road.
(3) If the deed or deeds to any of the lots do not provide for maintenance and repair of the access road(s) in accordance with the requirements set forth herein, then the cost of maintenance and repair of the access road(s) must be paid in equal shares by the owners of each of the lots depicted on the plat, and each such owner shall be responsible for seeing that such maintenance and repair is performed. If the county engineer, in his/her discretion, is satisfied that all of the conditions of this section have been met, then the plat may be submitted by the county engineer to the planning commission for approval or in those situations where permitted, to a licensed surveyor for certification. Columbia County shall not be responsible for construction, repair or maintenance of any access road unless the county has accepted ownership of the road in accordance with all requirements which have been established by the county.
(4) Any plat or map for which approval is sought under this section 74-42 of the Code must meet the requirements of O.C.G.A. § 15-6-67 in order that the clerk of superior court shall file and record in his/her office such maps and plats in the county. This will require approval by the county planning commission unless there is an exemption under [O.C.G.A.] § 15-6-67(d).
(5) Changes to plats depicting four lots or less must be made in accordance with the requirements set forth in subsection 74-40(4) of the Code.
(6) Lots or tracts of land resulting from the subdivision of land as depicted on a plat approved under this section, including the remaining portion of the original tract, may not be further subdivided under the provisions of this section for a period of five years after the date of the recording of the plat. If the original tract is subdivided into less than four lots as shown on the plat for which approval is sought, then the original tract may at a later date be subdivided further but only up to a grand total of not more than four lots being subdivided out of the original tract, including the original tract; provided that these subsequently subdivided lots may not be further subdivided for a period of five years after the date of the recording of the plat depicting their subdivision. The term "original tract," as used in this section, shall mean the entire tract of land as it existed immediately prior to the subdivision of any portion of such tract of land as depicted on the plat for which approval is being sought.
(Code 1979, § 2-13-24; Ord. No. 11-17, § 1, 11-1-2011; Ord. No. 14-04, § 1, 2-18-2014; Ord. No. 15-17, § 2, 6-16-2015)

1172:
(a) The subdivision of land creating lots abutting on private roads shall be permitted, provided that the:
(1) Private roads and the rights-of-way therefor are constructed and maintained in accordance with the requirements of this Code and minimum specifications therefor, as promulgated from time to time by the board of commissioners.
(2) Fee simple title to the rights-of-way for the roads are vested in the owners of the lots abutting such private roads, or a nonprofit state corporation of which all owners of lots having a right to use the roads are required by covenants running with the land to be members (referred to in this section as the "owner's association").
(3) Private roads are subject to a perpetual easement for ingress and egress to all of the lots in the subdivision, which easement shall be appurtenant to and pass with title to the lots in the subdivision.
(4) Owner's association shall, by covenants running with the land recorded in the office of the clerk of superior court, have the obligation to maintain the private roads and rights-of-way therefor in a good, safe and well-kept condition, and shall be required to levy annual assessments on lots in the subdivision to pay the cost thereof, and to establish and maintain reasonable reserves for future significant repair, rebuilding, repaving and maintenance of such roads, not required on an annual basis, which assessments, if unpaid, when due, become and continue to be a lien on the lot against which they were levied until they are paid.
(b) A subdivision of land creating lots fronting on private roads shall require approval of a preliminary plat and a final plat as set forth in this chapter for subdivisions using public roads, which shall be filed with the engineering services department for processing and consideration by the planning and zoning commission and the board of commissioners if any of the improvements located in such subdivision are to be dedicated to the county. At the time of the filing of the plat for preliminary approval, the owner of the land shall also file all legal instruments, including, but not limited to, grants of easements, declarations of covenants and articles of incorporation and bylaws of the owner's association, to be reviewed by the county attorney to determine if all of the requirements of subsection (a)(2), (a)(3) and (a)(4) of this section have been met. At the time of requesting final plat approval, a copy of the signed documents, with all exhibits attached, together with a certificate of incorporation for the owner's association from the secretary of state and a copy of the minutes of the organizational meeting of the owner's association certified by its secretary must be furnished to the county attorney for review.
(c) Subdivisions containing more than four lots, but not more than 12 lots, including the remaining portion of the original tract, access to which is provided by private roads, shall, at a minimum, provide access to the lots by not more than two private roads which must be at least 18 feet in width located within a right-of-way of not less than 30 feet in width, and built and paved in accordance with specifications established by the board of commissioners. If a subdivision is developed and access provided pursuant to the provisions of this subsection, the lots resulting from such subdivision, including the remaining portion of the original tract, may not be further subdivided without meeting all of the requirements of articles III and IV of this chapter for the development of subdivisions. Any subdivision containing more than 12 lots, access to which is provided by private roads, shall provide access to the lots by roads meeting all of the requirements of articles III and IV of this chapter for the development of subdivisions; provided, however, that if all of the lots in the subdivision are five acres or larger, the streets do not have to be paved, but must meet all other development construction standards. If all lots in the subdivision are 2.5 acres or larger, concrete curbs and gutters are not required. The term "original tract," as used in this subsection, means the entire tract of land as it existed immediately prior to the subdivision of any portion thereof as depicted on the plat for which approval is being sought.
(d) An appropriate permanent sign identifying the roads in the subdivision as private roads must be erected by the developer and maintained in good condition by the owner's association or the developer at all locations where private roads intersect with public roads.
(e) Subdivisions developed with the use of private roads must, except as specifically otherwise provided in this chapter, comply with all other requirements of this Code dealing with or relating to the subdivision of land and the construction of improvements on such land.
(f) No plat of a subdivision of land utilizing private roads for ingress and egress to the lots contained in such subdivision shall be approved unless it is in full compliance with the requirements of this section, unless a variance from any such requirement is granted by the board of commissioners.

1174:
(a) A performance and maintenance bond, letter of credit, cash bond, or other equivalent form of security as approved by the county attorney, running in favor of the county, in a minimum amount of $5,000.00 or any amount equal to at least ten percent of the actual construction cost of all improvements to be dedicated to the county, whichever is greater, shall be posted with the county by all subdividers or persons where street or other improvements are made and offered to the county for acceptance and maintenance except as noted in this section. The performance and maintenance bond, cash bond, letter of credit or other equivalent form of security shall guarantee all improvements against defects in design, material and workmanship and further guarantee that all such improvements shall be installed and maintained in first class condition for the required period and faithful performance by the subdivider or other person of all provisions of this chapter.
(1) Any bond, except cash bond, or letter of credit or other equivalent form of approved security shall be on forms supplied by the county and shall not be terminated or otherwise allowed to expire prior to the satisfactory completion of the maintenance period under section 74-46, or until released by the board of commissioners. (2) Such bond, cash bond, letter of credit or other equivalent form of security shall be posted prior to commencement of construction. No preliminary plat shall be approved or recorded by the county and no construction shall commence until and unless a satisfactory bond is posted.

1175:
(a) All subdivisions in which subdivider intends to dedicate all, or a portion of, the improvements located thereon to the county shall meet the requirements of this section. The subdivider shall maintain and repair all improvements, other than water and sewer, dedicated to the county for two years, unless extended pursuant to this section, from the date of written acceptance of the as-built drawings. The subdivider shall pay the reasonable costs for the county to maintain and repair all dedicated water and sewer improvements for two years, unless extended pursuant to this section.
(1) The subdivider shall request in writing that the county inspect the development at least 60 days prior to the expiration of the maintenance period. Failure to notify the county in writing shall extend the maintenance period until inspection is requested and all determined improvements are made.
(2) If upon inspection as provided in subsection (1) of this section, the county determines that work or repairs are needed in order for the improvements to meet county specifications or requirements under this chapter, the subdivider shall be notified in writing by the department of the deficiencies, failure to comply or violations. Thereafter, for deficiencies, failure to comply or violations related to improvements other than water and sewer, the subdivider shall extend the maintenance bond one year and shall have 60 days from receipt of such notification to correct such deficiencies, noncompliance or violations. If the deficiencies, noncompliance or violations are not corrected within such time, then the maintenance bond, cash bond, letter of credit or equivalent form of approved security posted by the subdivider shall be, if approved by the board of commissioners, forfeited and called upon up to the cost of the repairs or the total amount of the bond. Should the amount of the bond be inadequate to pay for the cost of correcting the deficiencies, noncompliance or violations, then the subdivider shall pay any and all costs beyond bond coverage. For deficiencies, failure to comply or violations related to water and sewer, the subdivider shall pay the county the reasonable cost to correct the same.
(3) The subdivider shall pay to the county for each inspection, subsequent to the initial inspection provided under subsection (1) of this section, a reinspection fee in an amount set from time to time by resolution of the board of commissioners to defray the cost of reinspection.
(4) The maintenance period shall continue until such time as the county has inspected and accepted the improvements in writing.
(5) If a period of 30 months elapses from the commencement of the maintenance period for any subdivision and defects, noncompliance or violations still exist to the extent that the subdivision has not been accepted by the county, the county is authorized to withhold the issuance of any and all permits or to refuse inspection to subdivider on the project in dispute and any other project in which the subdivider, or officer or owner thereof, has a financial interest.

1181:
(a) Location and width of streets and roads. The location and width of all streets and roads shall conform to the official major road plan as adopted by the planning commission.
(b) Connection of at least one existing street: At least one connecting street that terminates at, adjoins, or traverses a proposed subdivision and which will be used to provide access to the subdivision shall be a paved road not later than the approval of final plat for the first phase of the subdivision. If such access road is not a paved road it must be paved continuously in a manner meeting all of the requirements of this article from the nearest paved road on the public road system of the county, any adjoining county, any municipality located within the county or of the State of Georgia to at least one subdivision entrance. However, for those subdivisions that are creating lots under the provisions of section 74-42 of the Code, plats depicting subdivisions of four lots or less, and for those subdivisions that are creating lots larger than 15 acres under section 74-43 of the Code, subdivisions with private roads, at least one public road providing access to the subdivision shall be improved at least to the same standard as is required within the proposed subdivision from the nearest paved road on any of the public road systems described immediately above.
(c) Layout of new streets: The proposed street system within a subdivision shall be determined by the planning commission to adequately balance the privacy of the future occupants with the free flow of traffic within the county, and to adequately provide for access for public safety by fire, police and emergency medical vehicles, and for school buses. In making such determination, satisfaction of the following requirements shall be considered by the planning commission:
(1) In the opinion of the planning commission where it is necessary to provide for street access to adjoining property, proposed streets shall be extended by dedication and improvement of right-of-way to the boundary of such property.
(2) Unless approved otherwise by the planning commission, a subdivision shall provide a street connection to each public street that it adjoins, and shall provide direct or indirect continuity through the subdivision between each connection.
(3) The proposed street layout should be designed to minimize cut and fill within the right-of-way to provide better access to the subdivision lots. The design should also minimize the area of tree removal required for installation of streets, utilities and drainage features in order to reduce the number of large trees removed during construction.
(4) To the greatest extent practical, cul-de-sacs should be avoided in favor of loop streets or a curvilinear or grid system of streets.
(d) Reverse frontage lots:
(1) Except in the R-A Residential-Agricultural district reverse frontage lots shall be provided along all arterial and collector roads abutting a residential subdivision unless the planning commission specifically determines that the provision of such lots would create an unusual and burdensome hardship on the property owner due to topographic or dimensional disadvantages of the property. Reverse frontage lots shall not be required in the R-A Residential-Agricultural district where lots are platted with road frontage widths greater than 150 feet and driveways are separated by more than 300 feet unless the planning commission determines that limiting access to the collector or arterial street is necessary for safety reasons.
(2) An easement shall be provided to the county extending along the entire line of reverse frontage across which there shall be no right of access as follows:
a. Equal in depth to the minimum front building setback required by the zoning district. Within the easement existing vegetation shall remain or shall be supplemented or replaced by additional planting to provide substantial natural screening between the lots and the arterial and collector roads. Existing trees with ten inches diameter at breast height (dbh) or greater shall not be removed unless removal is approved by the county to prevent danger due to injury or disease to the tree; or
b. No less than 25 feet in depth and in accordance with the provisions and requirements of section 90-139, buffer requirements, of the zoning ordinance. Existing trees with ten inches diameter at breast height (dbh) or greater shall not be removed unless removal is approved by the county to prevent danger due to injury or disease to the tree.
(3) All buffer and landscaping treatments are subject to the review and approval of the planning commission. Modifications may be approved by the planning commission to achieve equivalent screening results, depending on the topography, orientation or other physical factors of the site.
(e) Interval of intersection with arteries. Subdivision streets which intersect an artery shall do so at intervals not less than the following:
(1) Limited access primary artery, 1,200 feet;
(2) Other primary artery, 800 feet; and
(3) Secondary artery, 400 feet.
(f) Large parcels. When land is subdivided into parcels larger than ordinary building lots, such parcels shall be arranged so as to allow for the opening of streets in the future, and for logical resubdivision.

1184:
(a) Adequate building sites. Each lot shall contain a building site not subject to flood or periodic inundation.
(b) Arrangement. Each lot must abut a public street or road. Side lot lines shall be at right angles to straight street lines or radial to curved street lines, where practical.
(c) Minimum lot dimensions and areas.
(1) The size and shape of lots shall meet the minimum standards set forth in the county's zoning regulations, chapter 90 of this Code, and orientation of lots shall be such as the planning commission deems appropriate for the use contemplated, type of water supply and sewage disposal, soil characteristics, improvements and relation to the street system.
(2) The minimum depths of building setback lines for lots platted for all purposes shall be subject to the provisions of the county zoning regulations, chapter 90 of this Code, as well as the following:
a. Wherever fill is proposed to raise land, the building setback line shall be located not less than 25 feet from the outer edge of the fill.
b. To prevent infringement of sight lines at intersections, the setback distances for corner lots shall be based on the minimum stopping sight distances for automobiles approaching the intersection as set forth in section 74-80. The building setback line for the corner lot shall not be closer to the street right-of-way line than that line which connects the two points located on the centerlines of the two streets, the prescribed minimum stopping sight distance from the center of the intersection.
(3) Properties reserved or platted for commercial or industrial purposes shall be adequate in size to provide for the off-street service and parking facilities required by the type of use and development contemplated. Platting of individual lots should be avoided in favor of an overall design of the land to be used for such purposes. Land shall not be platted for commercial or industrial purposes unless the subdivider can demonstrate to the planning commission:
a. A site arrangement that prevents undue interference with through traffic. Each industrial subdivision or area shall utilize a single collector for all heavy traffic between the area and the general system of streets and roads. Industrial streets and individual industrial parcels shall be oriented at right angles with the collector and with adjacent railroads;
b. An on-site parking area;
c. An insulation against any adverse effects on any present or future adjacent residences; and
d. A parcel size sufficient in area to allow future expansion.
(d) Double and reverse frontage lots.
Double and Reverse Frontage Lots
(1) Double frontage and reverse frontage lots should be avoided except where specifically required by the planning commission to provide separation of residential development from arterial and collector roads or to overcome specific disadvantages of topography and orientation of property.
(2) Reverse frontage lots shall be provided along all arterial and collector roads abutting a residential subdivision unless the planning commission specifically determines that the provision of such lots would create an unusual and burdensome hardship on the property owner due to topographic or dimensional disadvantages of the property.
(3) An easement to the county extending along the entire frontage, across which there shall be no right of access, and screening shall be provided along the line of reverse frontage lots abutting such arterial and collector roads, as follows:
a. In the R-A, residential-agricultural zoning district, the easement shall be equal in width to the minimum front building setback required by such zoning district. Within the easement, the existing vegetation shall be left undisturbed, but may be supplemented with additional plantings.
b. In all other residential zoning districts, the easement and screening shall be established as a buffer in accordance with the provisions and requirements of section 90-139 of this Code. The width of the buffer/easement for a natural buffer shall not be less than the minimum front building setback required by the zoning district in which it is located, or not less than 25 feet in width for a structural buffer if it creates an opaque screen to a height of not less than six feet.
c. All buffer and landscaping treatments are subject to the review and approval of the planning commission. Modifications may be approved by the planning commission to achieve equivalent screening results depending on the topography, orientation or other physical factors of the site.
(Code 1979, § 2-13-36(a)—(c); Ord. No. 00-7, § 2, 8-15-2000)
1185:
(a) Public open spaces. Where a school or recreation area, which is shown on an official map or in a plan made and adopted by the planning commission, is located in whole or in part in the applicant's subdivision, the planning commission may require the dedication or reservation of such open space within the subdivision, up to a total of ten percent of the gross area of the plot, including any water frontage for park, school or recreational purposes.
(b) Easements.
(1) Utilities. Except where alleys or rear service drives are permitted for such purpose, easements along rear and/or side lot lines, or elsewhere, if necessary, not exceeding 20 feet in width, shall be required for the extension of existing or planned utilities.
(2) Pedestrian. In cases and at such locations as the planning commission deems advisable, easements along side or rear lot lines, not exceeding 12 feet in width, may be required for pedestrian or bicycle traffic to and from schools, parks and other public places.
(3) Drainage. In cases in which a subdivision is traversed by a stream or drainage channel, there shall be provided a stormwater easement of such width along each side of the stream as the planning commission deems necessary for the purpose of widening, deepening, protecting, relocating or otherwise improving such drainage element.
(c) Community assets. In all subdivisions, due regard shall be shown for all natural features such as large trees and watercourses and for historical spots and similar community assets which, if preserved, will add attractiveness and value to the property.
(Code 1979, § 2-13-37)
1186:
In addition to the requirements set forth in section 74-117(b), any plan for subdividing property shall include the following:
(1) A plan showing the acreage of all on-site and off-site drainage areas contributing flow through the project.
(2) A hydrology report which shall include:
a. Minimum design frequency of a 25-year storm;
b. Minimum time of concentration of ten minutes;
c. Detailed calculations indicating the formula used;
d. Coefficient of run-off;
e. Time of concentration;
f. Rainfall intensity;
g. Discharged velocity; and
h. Source of all data used.
(3) Where the drainage area exceeds 150 acres, two formulas shall be used, and the average of the two shall be submitted.
(4) In addition to the requirements set forth in section 74-83(b)(3), the following shall also be required:
a. A five-foot easement along all side property lines.
b. A ten-foot easement along all rear property lines.
c. All storm drainage pipes shall be located within a ten-foot easement.
d. All stormwater discharged into natural drainage areas shall be as straight as possible.
e. All storm drainage pipes shall be at least 18 inches in diameter, and 18 inches below the surface, and shall have a slope of at least one percent.
f. Catchbasins shall be located at all low points of streets, and shall be located so as to service no more than four acres.
g. High water elevation contour based on a 25-year storm at the entrance of each head wall.
(5) To control erosion, all drainage easements, natural ditches and drainage areas shall be grassed and/or rip-rapped as necessary.
(6) All plans of subdivisions shall include a method of control so as to prevent the silting and/or erosion of natural drainage areas, natural drains and streams, and adjoining property. Such plans shall also provide for control of the rate of discharge of excess water.

Sidewalks may be required where deemed by the planning commission as an integral part of a pedestrian traffic system within a one-mile radius of existing or planned schools, neighborhood recreation or commercial areas or other public places. Where provided, sidewalks shall be located not less than one foot from the property line to prevent interference or encroachment by fencing, walls, hedges or other plantings or structures placed on the property line at a later date.
(e) Sanitary sewerage. In the areas of the county designated for sewerage service in the master sewerage plan prepared by the county engineer, all subdivision developers shall be required to install a sanitary sewerage collection system. The layout and specifications of the system shall be in accordance with the master sewerage plan and other applicable county specifications, and shall require the approval of the county engineer. Where sanitary sewerage collection systems are not specifically required by the county engineer, all lots shall contain adequate area for the installation and safe operation of approved septic tanks and disposal fields, and must be approved by the county health officer and other agencies having jurisdiction over such matters.
(f) Public water systems. Each subdivision developer shall be required to provide a potable water supply subject to the approval of the county health officer. (g) Site improvements. Banks which infringe on sight lines at intersections (see section 74-82(c)(2)) shall be appropriately graded to correct the deficiency. Wherever grading or filling occurs on lots within the subdivision, the subdivider shall first stockpile the topsoil from the affected areas immediately after grading and filling, and shall redistribute to areas of disturbed soil, sufficient topsoil to support growth of lawn grass and other vegetation, and shall immediately seed such areas with appropriate vegetative cover to prevent erosion, silting of streams and other damages. Due regard shall be shown for such desirable trees which are already on the site, and grading and filling should be planned to preserve as many of such trees possible; however, no retained planting shall infringe on sight lines at intersections. If trees are planted by the subdivider, they shall be located five feet inside or behind property lines where they are less subject to injury, decrease the chances of motor accidents and enjoy more favorable conditions for growth. If trees are to be planted within a planting strip in the right-of-way, the proposed locations and species of such trees to be used must be submitted for the planning commission's approval since the public inherits the care and maintenance of such trees. The planning commission will assist the subdivider in location of trees and species to use under varying conditions. Where land is platted or reserved for commercial or industrial use bordering and across minor streets from residential lots, a suitable buffer planting of trees and shrubs which are approved by the planning commission shall be required, and such trees and shrubs shall not infringe on sight lines at intersections where planted.
(h) Street name signs. Appropriate street signs add sales value to land subdivisions and enable strangers, delivery concerns and potential lot buyers to find their way around. Street name signs of a type approved by the county shall be placed at all intersections.

(Ord. No. 13-02, § 2, 4-2-2013)
1270:
(a) Such excise tax shall be levied and collected by the governing authority of Columbia County pursuant to O.C.G.A. §§ 48-13-112 and 48-13-114 and as provided in this section.
(b) Except as otherwise provided in this section, the rate of such excise tax shall be phased in over a four-year period as follows:
(1) For the period commencing January 1, 2013, and concluding at the last moment of December 31, 2013, such excise tax shall be at a rate equivalent to 25 percent of the total amount of local sales and use tax in effect in such special district that would be collected on the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy but for the exemption in O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2;
(2) For the period commencing January 1, 2014, and concluding at the last moment of December 31, 2014, such excise tax shall be at a rate equivalent to 50 percent of the total amount of local sales and use tax in effect in such special district that would be collected on the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy but for the exemption in O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2;
(3) For the period commencing January 1, 2015, and concluding at the last moment of December 31, 2015, such excise tax shall be at a rate equivalent to 75 percent of the total amount of local sales and use tax in effect in such special district that would be collected on the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy but for the exemption in O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2; and
(4) On or after January 1, 2016, such excise tax shall be at a rate equivalent to 100 percent of the total amount of local sales and use tax in effect in such special district that would be collected on the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy but for the exemption in O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2.
(c) In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2(c)(4), if a project of regional significance under O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3(92) is started in the special district, it shall not be subject to the phase-in period contained in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of subsection (b) of this section, and the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy in connection therewith shall be subject to the rate specified in paragraph (4) of subsection (b) of this section notwithstanding the January 1, 2016 limitation in that paragraph (4).
(d) (1) Following such initial imposition during the phase-in time period, on or after January 1, 2016, the rate of the excise tax levied and collected by the governing authority of Columbia County shall be directed by O.C.G.A. § 48-13-112(d). (3) In the event the total rate of local sales and use taxes in effect in the special district increases from one percent to two percent, the rate of the excise tax under this article shall likewise be increased at the same time such local sales and use tax rate increase becomes effective.

(a) Due date of tax. When any dealer fails to make any return or to pay the full amount of the tax required by an ordinance authorized by this article, there shall be imposed, in addition to other penalties provided by law, a penalty to be added to the tax in the amount of five percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, if the failure is for not more than 30 days and an additional five percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, for each additional 30 days or fraction of 30 days during which the failure continues.

1305:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to stop or stand, or for an owner to allow his vehicle to be parked in any handicapped parking place, unless there is displayed on the dashboard or hung from the rearview mirror of the parked vehicle a valid unexpired handicapped parking permit, or unless there is attached to the parked vehicle a specially designated license plate for disabled persons authorized under O.C.G.A. § 40-6-222(d).

1321:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Axle means a supporting shaft or member on which a wheel or pair of wheels revolves.
Boat means a craft designed to float on water.
Box truck means a self-powered, single unit vehicle with fully or partially enclosed cuboid space in which the cargo area is connected to the cabin by a single chassis or frame; refrigerated or unrefrigerated.
Bus means every motor vehicle designed for carrying more than 15 passengers.
Camper trailer means a trailer as defined in this section, which is pulled behind a motorized vehicle, and is used for recreational camping as a shelter or carrier for equipment.
Food truck means any motor vehicle, mobile vending unit, or trailer, equipped for storing, transporting, cooking, preparing, serving or selling food.
Home occupation vehicle means an allowed vehicle used as part of a licensed home occupation pursuant to section 90-142. Allowed vehicles include standard passenger vehicles, utility trailers, box trucks, food trucks, and trucks with service bodies or holding towing permits and specifically exclude tractor units or tractor trailers, dump trucks, concrete trucks, towing haulers, and other large vehicles.
Inoperative vehicle means a vehicle that cannot be driven upon public streets for any reasons including but not limited to being unlicensed, wrecked, abandoned, discarded, in a state of disrepair, partially dismantled, or incapable of being moved under its own power.
Large vehicle means flatbed trucks, dump trucks, concrete trucks, towing haulers, vehicles with service bodies or vehicles holding a towing permit or any large vehicle exceeding 10,000 pounds.
Limousine means any motor vehicle that meets the manufacturer's specifications for a luxury limousine with a designed seating capacity for no more than ten passengers and with a minimum of five seats located behind the operator of the vehicle, and which does not have a door at the rear of the vehicle designed to allow passenger entry or exit. No vehicle shall be permitted to be operated as both a taxicab and a limousine.
Motor home means a motor vehicle built on a truck or bus chassis, and which is equipped to serve as self-contained living quarters for recreational travel.
Owner, whenever used in this division in relation to parking a motor vehicle, shall mean and include the titled owner, any person who has purchased the vehicle but not yet applied for title in his name, any operator of the vehicle, any person renting the vehicle and any person who operates a vehicle owned by, and on behalf of, a business, partnership or corporation.
Portable storage container means a self-storage container that is delivered to and retrieved from a home or business for long term off-site or on-site storage. Portable on demand storage or PODS are a familiar trade name for such containers. These containers are not on a chassis and do not have axles or wheels.
Temporary storage container means a portable storage unit that does not have a permanent foundation or footing and which includes cargo containers, portable storage containers, truck trailers, construction trailers, and bulk solid waste containers. Such portable structures shall not be considered a building and specifically exclude "handy houses" and similar units.
Trailer means a transport vehicle designed to be hauled by an automobile, truck or tractor unit.
Tractor unit means a heavy-duty towing engine that provides motive power for hauling a towed or trailered load, including but not limited to a semi-trailer.
Truck means a motorized vehicle designed and/or used for transporting loads.
Vehicle means a device, such as a motor vehicle or a piece of mechanized equipment, used for transporting passengers, goods, apparatuses or equipment.
Wrecker means any truck or other vehicle which is used to move or transport disabled, abandoned or other vehicles.
(Ord. No. 16-05, § 1(Exh. A), 3-29-2016; Ord. No. 25-01, § 1(Exh. A), 2-18-2025)

1322:

1333:
The sheriff shall establish a call list for each of the three classes of wrecker vehicles set forth in section 82-177. The operators listed on such call list shall be called for assistance by the sheriff's department or other county officials, as needed, on a rotating basis, with the class of wrecker vehicle being called to the scene which is most appropriately designed and equipped to handle the vehicles which are to be towed. The call list for each class of wrecker vehicles shall include not more than 12 operators. If a call list is full, the sheriff shall place operators who apply for inclusion on the call list on a waiting list with priority on the waiting list being based on the date the application is filed with the sheriff, the earliest application date being the date of higher priority, subject, however, to the provisions of section 82-184. The sheriff shall promulgate, and may amend from time to time, policies, procedures, rules and regulations for the establishment and use of the call list which shall be consistent with the provisions of this article, but which may contain additional requirements for inclusion of operators on the call list, and the operation and use of the call list which the sheriff finds to be in the best interest of the public, for the protection of the public, for the safe, prompt and efficient removal of disabled or abandoned vehicles from public roads, and the cleanup of accident sites, and for otherwise safe and efficient towing of vehicles as required by the county and the sheriff.
(Code 1979, § 2-15-26; Ord. of 11-2-1993)
1334:
No operator shall be placed on the call list as set forth in section 82-178 prior to obtaining a towing permit from the county, as provided for in this article, for each wrecker vehicle used by such operator. Permits will be issued for class A, B and C wrecker vehicles, depending on which of the requirements set forth in section 82-177 the wrecker vehicle being permitted meets.
(Code 1979, § 2-15-27; Ord. of 11-2-1993)
1335:
(a) Any operator desiring to obtain a towing permit for a wrecker vehicle shall file with the wrecker inspector an application setting out the following:
(1) Name, business address, business telephone number, home address and home telephone number of the operator seeking the permit.
(2) The business address at which the wrecker vehicle for which the application is being made is based, and a description of the buildings, fenced storage area and other facilities located at such address which are utilized in connection with the wrecker towing business.
(3) The number of wrecker vehicles available for use by the applicant, and the towing permit numbers of each vehicle, if towing permits have been previously used for such wrecker vehicles.
(4) A full description of the wrecker vehicles for which a towing permit is being sought, with sufficient information to determine the proper classification of each wrecker vehicle.
(5) A statement that all wrecker vehicles for which a permit is being sought are properly equipped for the classification for which the permit is sought, and in accordance with the requirements of this article.
(6) A statement that the operator, when included on the call list, will:
a. Provide 24-hour service, including holidays;
b. Have a qualified driver on duty at all times; and
c. Release a vehicle to its rightful owner at any time of the day or night upon 45 minutes' prior notice.
(7) A statement that the operator will accept responsibility for all personal property left in towed or stored vehicles.
(8) Attach to the application a certificate of insurance evidencing that the applicant has the minimum amounts of insurance required under state and federal regulations then in effect for motor carriers operating freight equipment, which certificate of insurance must contain an endorsement providing for a minimum of ten days' notice to the sheriff prior to the effective date of any cancellation of the policy evidenced by such certificate.
(9) Attach to the permit application a copy of the applicant's current county business license for the wrecker towing business, and a statement from the county zoning administration that the real property in the county used by the applicant for the wrecker towing business is properly zoned for such use.
(b) The wrecker inspector shall, upon determining that a permit application is complete, inspect the applicant's place of business and the towing vehicles for which a towing permit is sought, to verify that the applicant has the required vehicles, equipment and facilities to authorize the issuance of the towing permit being sought, and to confirm that the applicant is operating in compliance with all applicable state and federal safety regulations pertaining to the operation of a wrecker towing business. No towing permit shall be issued until the operator has demonstrated, to the satisfaction of the wrecker inspector, that the operator meets all of the requirements for the towing permit applied for as set forth in subsection (a) of this section and in the regulations.
(Code 1979, § 2-15-28; Ord. of 11-2-1993)
1336:
(a) In addition to the equipment required under the applicable wrecker vehicle classifications as set forth in section 82-177, all wrecker vehicles for which a towing permit is issued shall have and maintain the following equipment, as a condition to issuance of the permit:
(1) At least one heavy-duty push broom.
(2) One shovel.

(4) At least one spare fuse or other overload protective device if the devices used are not of a reset type for each kind and size used.
(5) Three bidirectional emergency reflective triangles.
(6) Tow lights.
(7) One set of bolt cutters.

The fenced storage area must be large enough to park not less than 30 full-size passenger cars.
(Code 1979, § 2-15-29; Ord. of 11-2-1993)
1337:
The operator shall not employ or authorize anyone, including the operator, to drive a wrecker vehicle who does not meet the qualifications for drivers established by the United States Department of Transportation, Federal Highway Administration, and Safety Regulations Parts 383 and 391. Medical examinations must be performed at least once every two years on the drivers of wrecker vehicles operating under towing permits issued pursuant to this article, in accordance with the procedures for testing as set forth in FMCSR Sections 391.41, 391.43 and 391.45.
(Code 1979, § 2-15-30; Ord. of 11-2-1993)
1338:
If the wrecker inspector approves an application for issuance of a towing permit, he shall forward written evidence of such approval to the office of the county designated by the board of commissioners to issue towing permits, which office shall promptly issue the approved towing permit. The towing permit shall be kept on board the wrecker vehicle for which it was issued. A towing permit shall be in effect until December 31 of the year in which it was issued, at which time it shall expire and a new towing permit will have to be applied for.
(Code 1979, § 2-15-31; Ord. of 11-2-1993)
1339:
(a) The wrecker inspector or the sheriff may suspend or revoke the towing permit for any wrecker vehicle on any of the following grounds:
(1) If the towing permit was procured by fraudulent, false or misleading statements, conduct or representations.
(2) Failure of the operator to comply with state and federal safety regulations applicable to the operation of a wrecker towing business.
(3) Failure of the operator to comply with the provisions of this article or the regulations.
(4) Failure of the operator to maintain the insurance coverages as set forth in section 82-180(a)(8).
(5) Failure of the operator to maintain and operate such wrecker vehicle in accordance with the requirements of state and federal regulations pertaining to the maintenance and operation of the vehicle.
(6) An unsatisfactory or conditional rating by the United States Department of Transportation.
(b) A suspension of a towing permit may be for a period of not less than 30 days, nor more than 180 days. If an operator's towing permit is suspended, the operator shall be removed from the call list during such period of suspension, but shall be returned to the call list when the suspension is lifted, provided that the call list does not have at that time 12 operators on it. If there are 12 operators on the call list upon the lifting of the suspension, the affected operator will be placed at the top of the waiting list.
(c) A revocation of a towing permit shall automatically cause the operator to be removed from the call list. Once removed from the call list because of a revocation of the towing permit, the operator shall be treated as a new applicant for inclusion on the call list if he subsequently acquires a permit and again becomes eligible to be placed on the call list. Any operator who has a towing permit revoked shall not be eligible to apply for a towing permit for a period of one year following such revocation.
(d) The suspension or revocation of one or more towing permits held by an operator shall automatically operate as a suspension or revocation, as the case may be, of all permits held by such operator.
(Code 1979, § 2-15-32; Ord. of 11-2-1993)
1340:
(a) Unless otherwise provided in this article, or unless waived by the holder of a towing permit, no towing permit shall be suspended or revoked without the opportunity for a hearing as provided in this section. The wrecker inspector shall provide written notice to the operator of the initiation of an action to suspend or revoke a towing permit. Such written notification shall set forth, in reasonable detail, the reasons for such action, and shall notify the operator of the right to a hearing under the provisions of this section. Any operator against whom action for the suspension or revocation of a towing permit is initiated may have a hearing concerning such action before the sheriff or his designee. Such hearing shall be by written request filed with the sheriff within ten days after the date of the notice of the initiation of the action from the wrecker inspector to the operator. Such written request for a hearing shall set forth the reasons why the operator feels that the proposed action should not be taken, and in reasonable detail, the grounds and facts which the operator contends support the operator's position. The sheriff or his designee shall determine whether or not the towing permit shall be temporarily suspended during the period prior to the hearing, and until final action is taken by the sheriff or his designee. Failure of the operator to request a hearing within the specified time shall be deemed to be a waiver by the operator of a right to a hearing, and the sheriff or his designee shall be authorized to proceed with final action on the matter without the holding of a hearing.
(b) If requested, a hearing shall be held not less than ten days, nor more than 45 days after the date of the filing of the request for a hearing with the sheriff. At such hearing, the operator shall have the right to be represented by an attorney, at the expense of the operator, and to present evidence and cross examine witnesses.
(c) The action of the sheriff or his designee shall be forwarded to the wrecker inspector within 15 days after the conclusion of the hearing, and the wrecker inspector shall notify the operator by certified mail, return receipt requested, of the action taken by the sheriff or his designee. When taken, the action taken by the sheriff or his designee shall be final.
(Code 1979, § 2-15-33; Ord. of 11-2-1993)
1341:
The board of commissioners shall, by resolution, set filing fees for the filing of an application for a towing permit. Such fees shall be in an amount that the board of commissioners, in its discretion, shall determine, shall be sufficient to cover the costs incurred by the county in receiving and processing an application for and issuance of a towing permit, and shall be set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file in the office of the county clerk. Such fees shall be payable at the time that the towing permit application is filed, and such fees shall not be prorated if the permit will be valid for less than a full calendar year. The board of commissioners, in its discretion, may set lower fees for renewal permits if it determines that the cost of receiving and processing renewal applications is less than for the first time towing permit.

1365:
(a) Purpose.
(1) To protect the public potable water supply served by the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services from the possibility of contamination or pollution by containment, within its customers internal distribution system, such contaminants or pollutants which could backflow or back-siphon into the public water system.
(2) To promote the elimination or control of existing cross-connections, actual or potential, between its customers in-plant potable water system, and non-potable systems.
(3) To provide for the maintenance of a continuing program of cross-connection control which will effectively prevent the contamination or pollution of all potable water systems by cross-connection.
(b) Authority.
(1) The Federal Safe Drinking Water Act of 1974, and the statutes of the State of Georgia Chapters 391-3-5.13 the water purveyor has the primary responsibility for preventing water from unapproved sources, or any other substances, from entering the public potable water system.
(2) Columbia County Water Utility, Rules and Regulations, adopted.
(c) Responsibility. The director of water and sewer services shall be responsible for the protection of the public potable water distribution system from contamination or pollution due to the backflow or backsiphonage of contaminants or pollutants through the water service connection. If, in the judgment of the director of the water and sewer services, an approved backflow device is required at the county's water service connection to any customer's promises, the director, or his delegated agent, shall give notice in writing to said customer to install an approved backflow prevention device at each service connection to his premises. The customer shall, within 90 days install such approved device, or devices, at his own expense, and failure or refusal, or inability on the part of the customer to install said device or devices within 90 days, shall constitute a ground for discontinuing water service to the premises until such device or devices have been properly installed. Backflow assemblies are to be installed by a licensed plumber, licensed fire protection system installer, and/or licensed underground utility contractor on all new installations only. Backflow assemblies that are retrofits and upgrades must be installed by a licensed plumber. All repairs are to be made by a licensed master plumber or someone certified by the State of Georgia in backflow device repair. The device requires an initial test within five days of installation and then annually tested by a certified backflow tester to assure that it is functioning correctly and forwarded to the compliance office.
(d) Definitions.
Approved. Accepted by the director of the water and sewer services as meeting an applicable specification stated or cited in this regulation, or as suitable for the proposed use.
Auxiliary water supply. Any water supply, on or available, to the premises other than the purveyor's approved public potable water supply.
Backflow. The flow of water or other liquids, mixtures or substances, under positive or reduced pressure in the distribution pipes of a potable water supply from any source other than its intended source.
Backflow preventer. A device or means designed to prevent backflow or backsiphonage. Most commonly categorized as air gap, reduced pressure principle device, double check valve assembly, pressure vacuum breaker, atmospheric vacuum breaker, hose bibb vacuum breaker, residential dual check, double check with intermediate atmospheric vent, and barometric loop.
(1) Air gap. A physical separation sufficient to prevent backflow between the free-flowing discharge end of the potable water system and any other system. Physically defined as a distance equal to twice the diameter of the supply side pipe diameter but never less than one inch.
(2) Atmospheric vacuum breaker. A device which prevents backsiphonage by creating an atmospheric vent when there is either a negative pressure or sub-atmospheric pressure in a water system.
(3) Double check valve assembly. An assembly of two independently operating spring loaded check valves with tightly closing shut off valves on each side of the check valves, plus properly located test cocks for the testing of each check valve.
(4) Hose bibb vacuum breaker. A device which is permanently attached to a hose bibb and which acts as an atmospheric vacuum breaker.
(5) Pressure vacuum breaker. A device containing one or two independently operated spring loaded check valves and an independently operated spring loaded air inlet valve located on the discharge side of the check or checks. Device includes tightly closing shut-off valves on each side of the check valves and properly located test cocks for the testing of the check valve(s).
(6) Reduced pressure principle backflow preventer. An assembly consisting of two independently operating approved check valves with an automatically operating differential relief valve located between the two check valves, tightly closing shut-off valves on each side of the check valves plus properly located test cocks for the testing of the check valves and the relief valve.
(7) Residential dual check. An assembly of two spring loaded, independently operating check valves without tightly closing shut-off valves and test cocks. Generally employed immediately downstream of the water meter to act as a containment device.
Backpressure. A condition in which the owners system pressure is greater than the suppliers system pressure.
Backsiphonage. The flow of water or other liquids, mixtures or substances into the distribution pipes of a potable water supply system from any source other than its intended source caused by the sudden reduction of pressure in the potable water supply system.
Commissioners. Columbia County Board of Commissioners.
Containment. A method of backflow prevention which requires a backflow prevention preventer at the water service entrance.
Contaminant. A substance that will impair the quality of the water to a degree that it creates a serious health hazard to the public leading to poisoning or the spread of disease.
Cross-connection. Any actual or potential connection between the public water supply and a source of contamination or pollution.
Department. Columbia County Water and Sewer Services.
Director of water and sewer services. The director, or his delegated representative in charge of the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services, is invested with the authority and responsibility for the implementation of a cross-connection control program and for the enforcement of the provisions of the chapter.
DNR. Department of Natural Resource.
EPD. Environmental Protection Division.
Fixture isolation. A method of backflow prevention in which a backflow preventer is located to correct a cross-connection at an in-plant location rather than at a water service entrance.
Owner. Any person, who has legal title to, or license to operate or habitat in, a property upon which a cross-connection inspection is to be made or upon which a cross-connection is present.
Person. Any individual, partnership, company, public or private corporation, political subdivision or agency of the state department, agency or instrumentality or the United States or any other legal entity.
Permit. A document issued by the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services Compliance Office which allows the use of a backflow preventer.
Pollutant. A foreign substance, that if permitted to get into the public water system, will degrade its quality so as to constitute a moderate hazard, or impair the usefulness or quality of the water to a degree which does not create an actual hazard to the public health but which does adversely and unreasonably effect such water for domestic use.
Water service entrance. That point in the owners water system beyond the sanitary control of the district; generally considered to be the outlet end of the water meter and always before any unprotected branch.
(e) Administration.
(1) The Columbia County Water and Sewer Services will operate a cross-connection control program, to include the keeping of necessary records, which fulfills the requirements of the commission's cross-connection regulations and is approved by the commission.
(2) The owner shall allow his property to be inspected for possible cross-connections and shall follow the provisions of the department's program and the commission's regulations if a cross-connection is permitted.
(3) If the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services requires that the public supply be protected by containment, the owner shall be responsible for water quality beyond the outlet end of the containment device and should utilize fixture outlet protection for that purpose.
He may utilize public health officials, or personnel from the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services, or their delegated representatives, to assist him in the survey of his facilities and to assist him in the selection of proper fixture outlet devices, and the proper installation of these devices.
(f) Requirements.
(1) Columbia County Water Utility.
a. On new installations, the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services will provide on-site evaluation and/or inspection of plans in order to determine the type of backflow preventer, if any, that will be required, will issue permit, and perform inspection and testing. In any case, a minimum of a double check valve with a wye strainer will be required in any new commercial construction and a minimum of a dual check on any residential.
b. For premises existing prior to the start of this program, the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services will perform evaluations and inspections of plans and/or premises and inform the owner by letter of any corrective action deemed necessary, the method of achieving the correction, and the time allowed for the correction to be made. Ordinarily, 90 days will be allowed, however, this time period may be shortened depending upon the degree of hazard involved and the history of the device(s) in question.
c. The Columbia County Water and Sewer Services will not allow any cross-connection to remain unless it is protected by an approved backflow preventer for which a permit has been issued and which will be regularly tested to insure satisfactory operation.
d. If the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services determines at any time that a serious threat to the public health exists, the water service will be terminated immediately.
e. The Columbia County Water and Sewer Services shall have on file, a list of private contractors who are certified backflow device testers. All charges for these tests will be paid by the owner of the building or property.
f. The Columbia County Water and Sewer Services requires all reduced pressure principle devices and double check valve backflow preventers include the installation of strainers located immediately upstream of the backflow device. The installation of strainers will preclude the fouling of backflow devices due to both foreseen and unforeseen circumstances occurring to the water supply system such as water main repairs, water main breaks, fires, periodic cleaning, and flushing of mains, etc. These occurrences may "stir up" debris within the water main that will cause fouling of backflow devices installed without the benefit of strainers.
(2) Owner.
a. The owner shall be responsible for the elimination or protection of all cross-connections on his premises.
b. The owner, after having been informed by a letter from the department, shall at his expense, install, maintain, and test, or have tested, any and all backflow preventers on his premises.
c. The owner shall correct any malfunction of the backflow preventer which is revealed by periodic testing.
d. The owner shall inform the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services of any proposed or modified cross-connections and also any existing cross-connections of which the owner is aware but has not been found by the department.
e. The owner shall not install a bypass around any backflow preventer unless there is a backflow preventer of the same type on the bypass. Owners who cannot shut down operation for testing of the device(s) must supply additional devices necessary to allow testing to take place.
f. The owner shall install backflow preventers in a manner approved by the Columbia County Water Utility.
g. The owner shall install only backflow preventers approved by the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services or the EPD.
h. Any owner having a private well or other private water source, must have a permit if the well or source is cross-connected to the Columbia County Water Utility's system. Permission to cross-connect may be denied by the Columbia County Water Utility. The owner may be required to install a backflow preventer at the service entrance if a private water source is maintained, even if it is not cross-connected to the Columbia County Water Utility's system.
i. In the event the owner installs plumbing to provide potable water for domestic purposes which is on the Columbia County Water Utility's side of the backflow preventer, such plumbing must have its own backflow preventer installed.
j. The owner shall be responsible for the payment of all fees for permits, annual or semi-annual device testing, retesting in the case that the device fails to operate correctly, and second re-inspections for non-compliance with the Columbia County Water Utility.
(g) Degree of hazard. The Columbia County Water and Sewer Services recognizes the threat to the public water system arising from cross-connections. All threats will be classified by degree of hazard and will require the installation of approved reduced pressure principle backflow prevention devices or double check valves.
(h) Permits. The Columbia County Water and Sewer Services shall not permit a cross-connection within the public water supply system unless it is considered necessary and that it cannot be eliminated.
(1) Cross-connection permits that are required for each backflow prevention device are obtained from the Columbia County Water Utility.
(2) Permits shall be renewed annually and are non-transferable. Permits are subject to revocation and become immediately revoked if the owner should so change the type of cross-connection or degree of hazard associated with the service.
(3) An initial inspection permit is required on new residential dual check backflow preventer.
(i) Existing in-use backflow prevention devices. Any existing backflow preventer shall be allowed by the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services to continue in service unless the degree of hazard is such as to supersede the effectiveness of the present backflow preventer, or result in an unreasonable risk to the public health. Where the degree of hazard has increased, an in the case of a residential installation converting to a business establishment, any existing backflow preventer must be upgraded to a reduced pressure principle device, or a reduced pressure principle device must be installed in the event that no backflow device was present.
(j) Periodic testing.
(1) All backflow devices shall be tested and inspected at least annually.
(2) Testing must be performed by licensed backflow tester approved by the State of Georgia.
(3) Any backflow preventer which fails during a periodic test will be repaired or replaced at owner's expense. When repairs are necessary, upon completion of the repair the device will be retested at owner's expense to insure correct operation. High hazard situations will not be allowed to continue unprotected if the backflow preventer fails the test and cannot be repaired immediately. In other situations, a compliance date of not more than 30 days after the test date will be established. The owner is responsible for spare parts, repair tools, or a replacement device. Parallel installation of two devices is an effective means of the owner insuring that uninterrupted water service during testing or repair of devices and is strongly recommended when the owner desires such continuity. Backflow prevention devices will be tested more frequently than specified in subsection (1), above, in cases where there is a history of test failures and the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services feels that due to the degree of hazard involved, additional testing is warranted. Cost of the additional tests will be borne by the owner.
(k) Records and reports.
(1) Records. The Columbia County Water and Sewer Services will initiate and maintain the following:
a. Master files on customer cross-connection tests and/or inspections.
b. Master files on cross-connection permits.
c. Copies of permits and permit applications.
d. Copies of lists and summaries supplied to the EPD.
(2) Reports. The Columbia County Water and Sewer Services will submit the following to the EPD.
a. Initial listing of low hazard cross-connections to the state.
b. Initial listing of high hazard cross-connections to the state.
c. Annual update lists of subsection a. and b. above.
d. Annual summary of cross-connection inspections to the state.
(l) Fees and charges.
(1) The Columbia County Board of Commissioners has established fees under this article or charges for the following services or permits:
a. Initial inspection fees.
b. Annual inspection fees.
c. Water trucks and tank permit fee.
d. Citations and violations.
(2) A list of the fees is on file at the clerk of court and the Columbia County Water Utility.
(3) The fees for such inspections shall be issued for a period of one year. All permits will expire at 12:00 midnight on the date specified on the permit as determined by the Columbia County Water Utility.
(4) Citations and violations for lack of compliance will be determined and applied to the inspection fee.
(m) Water trucks and tanks inspection and permit fee.
(1) Water trucks and tanks shall be inspected annually by Columbia County Water and Sewer Services and be issued a permit number and decal that shall be placed on the tank.
(2) Water trucks and tanks shall have a RFZ backflow assembly or an air gap two times the diameter of the fill pipe and not less than one inch.
(3) The fees for such inspections shall be issued for a period of one year. All permits will expire at 12:00 midnight on the date specified on the permit as determined by the Columbia County Water Utility.
(4) Citations for lack of compliance will be determined.
(5) The Columbia County Board of Commissioners has established fees under this article or charges for the following services or permits:
a. Potable water trucks inspection.
b. Non-potable water trucks inspection.
c. Mobile tanks inspection.
(6) A list of the fees is on file at the clerk of commission and the business office of Columbia County Water Utility.

Building sewer means the extension from a building drain to the public sewer or other place of disposal, also known as house connection or service connection.
Categorical pretreatment standard and categorical standard mean any regulation containing pollutant discharge limits promulgated by the EPA in accordance with section 307(b) and (c) of the Act (33 USC § 1317) which applies to a specific category of users, and which appear in 40 CFR 405—471, chapter I, subchapter N.
Commission and county commission mean the board of commissioners of the county, which has jurisdiction over the maintenance and operations of the water and sanitary sewer system within the county.
Director means the director of the county water utility services division.
Environmental protection division and EPD mean the state department of natural resources division, environmental protection division.
Existing source means any source of discharge, the construction or operation of which commenced prior to the publication by the EPA of the proposed categorical pretreatment standards, which will be applicable to such source if the standard is promulgated in accordance with section 307 of the Act.
Filtration/inflow means groundwater and surface water which leaks into the sewers through cracked pipes, joints, manholes or other openings.
Floatable oil means oil, fat or grease in a physical state such that it will separate by gravity from wastewater by treatment in an approved pretreatment facility. Wastewater shall be considered free of floatable oil if it is properly pretreated in an approved grease trap, and the wastewater does not interfere with the POTW.
Food service establishment means any restaurant, eatery, food caterer, cafeteria, hospital, school, institution, motel, hotel, prison, business or similar place, other than dwelling units, where food is prepared for sale, delivery or consumption.
Garbage means the animal and vegetable waste resulting from the handling, preparation, cooking and serving of food.
Grab sample means a sample which is taken from a waste stream without regard to the flow in the waste stream. The sample may be taken over a period of time not to exceed 15 minutes.
Grease trap means a device primarily used in the food service industry for removal of oil, grease and food solids from a process prior to discharge into the POTW.
Indirect discharge means the introduction of pollutants into the POTW from any nondomestic source regulated under section 307(b), (c) or (d) of the Act.
Industrial user means a nonresidential user identified in Division A, B, C, D, E or I of the standard industrial classification. This term shall also include any significant industrial user.
Industrial waste means the wastewater from industrial processes as distinct from domestic or sanitary wastes.
Interference means a discharge, which alone or in conjunction with discharges from other sources, which inhibits or disrupts the POTW or public sewer, its treatment processes or operations, or its sludge processes, use or disposal, and therefore, is a cause of a violation of the county's NPDES permit or of the prevention of sewerage sludge use or disposal in compliance with the following statutory/regulatory provisions or permits issued under the NPDES permit, or any more stringent state or local regulations: Section 405 of the act; the SWDA; and state regulations contained in any state sludge management plan prepared pursuant to Subtitle D of the SWDA; the Clean Air Act, 42 USC § 7401 et seq.; the Toxic Substances Control Act, 15 USC § 2601 et seq.; and the Marine Protection, Research and Sanctuaries Act, 16 USC § 1361 et seq.
Mass emission rate means the weight of material discharged to the public sewer during a given time interval. Unless otherwise specified in this article, the mass emission rate shall mean pounds per day (lbs./d) of a particular constituent or combination of constituents.
Medical waste means isolation wastes, infectious agents, human blood and blood products, pathological wastes, sharps, body parts, contaminated bedding, surgical wastes, potentially contaminated laboratory wastes and dialysis wastes.
May is permissive.
National categorical pretreatment standard and pretreatment standard mean a regulation containing pollutant discharge limits applicable to a specific category of industrial users, promulgated by the EPA in accordance with section 307(b) and (c) of the Act (33 USC § 1317). This term includes prohibited discharge limits established pursuant to 40 CFR 403.5.
National Pollution Discharge Elimination System permit and NPDES permit mean a permit issued pursuant to section 402 of the Act (33 USC § 1342).
Natural outlet means a discharge into a watercourse, pond, ditch, lake or other body of surface water or groundwater.
New source means:
(1) A building, structure, facility or installation from which there is a discharge of pollutants, the construction of which commenced after the publication of proposed pretreatment standards under section 307(c) of the Act, which will be applicable to such source if such standards are thereafter promulgated in accordance with such section, provided that the:
a. Building, structure, facility or installation is constructed at a site at which no other source is located;
b. Building, structure, facility or installation totally replaces the process or production equipment that causes the discharge of pollutants at an existing source; or
c. Production or wastewater generating processes of the building, structure, facility or installation are substantially independent of an existing source at the same site.
In determining whether these are substantially independent, factors such as the extent to which the new facility is integrated with the existing plant and the extent to which the new facility is engaged in the same general type of activity as the existing source should be considered.
(2) Construction on a site at which an existing source is located results in a modification rather than a new source if the construction does not create a new building, structure, facility or installation meeting the criteria of subsection (1)b. or (1)c. of this definition, but otherwise alters, replaces or adds to existing process or production equipment.

a. Begun, or caused to begin, as part of a continuous on-site construction program:
1. Any placement, assembly or installation of facilities or equipment; or
2. Significant site preparation work including clearing, excavation or removal of existing buildings, structures or facilities which is necessary for the placement, assembly or installation of new source facilities or equipment; or
b. Entered into a binding contractual obligation for the purchase of facilities or equipment which are intended to be used in its operation within a reasonable time. Options to purchase or contracts which can be terminated or modified without substantial loss, and contracts for feasibility, engineering and design studies do not constitute a contractual obligation under this definition.
Noncontact cooling water means water used for cooling which does not come into direct contact with any raw material, intermediate product, waste product or finished product.
Pass through means a discharge which exits the POTW into waters of the United States in quantities or concentrations which, alone or in conjunction with discharges from other sources, is a cause of violation of any requirement of the county's NPDES permit, including an increase in the magnitude or duration of a violation.
pH means a measure of the acidity or alkalinity of a solution, expressed in standard units (grams per liter of solution).

Pollution means the manmade or man-induced alteration of the chemical, physical, biological or radiological integrity of water.

Pretreatment requirement means any substantive or procedural requirement related to pretreatment imposed on a user, other than a national pretreatment standard.

Prohibited discharge standards or discharges mean absolute prohibitions against the discharge of certain substances which are set forth in section 86-133.
Publicly owned treatment works and POTW mean treatment works as defined by section 212 of the Act (33 USC § 1292), which are owned by the county. Representative sample means a portion of wastewater that is small enough in volume to be transported conveniently while accurately displaying the characteristics of the wastewater being sampled.
Residential user means a premises used for human residency or habitation.
Sanitary wastewater means wastewater discharged into the POTW from the sanitary conveniences of dwellings, office buildings, industrial plants or institutions.
Septic tank means a sewage disposal tank in which a continuous flow of waste material is decomposed by anaerobic bacteria.
Sewage means human excrement and gray water (household showers, dish washing operations, etc.).
Significant industrial user means a user which:
(1) a. Is subject to categorical pretreatment standards;
b. Has in its waste a toxic pollutant in toxic amounts as defined in standards issued under section 307(a) of the Act;
c. Discharges an average of 25,000 gpd or more of process wastewater to the POTW, excluding sanitary, noncontact cooling water, sanitary and boiler blow down wastewater;
d. Contributes a process waste stream which makes up five percent or more of the average dry weather hydraulic or organic capacity of the POTW treatment plant; or
e. Is designated as such by the county on the basis that it has a reasonable potential or in combination with other contributing industries for adversely affecting the POTW's operation or for violating any pretreatment standard or requirement.
(2) Upon finding that a user meeting the criteria in subsections (1)b. and c. of this definition has no reasonable potential for adversely affecting the POTW's operation or for violating any pretreatment standard or requirement, the county may, at any time, on its own initiative or in response to a petition received from a user and in accordance with procedures set forth in 40 CFR 403.8(f)(6), determine that such user should not be considered a significant industrial user.
Significant noncompliance means:
(1) Chronic violations of wastewater discharge limits, which are defined as those in which 66 percent or more of wastewater measurements taken during a six-month period exceed the daily maximum limit or average limit for the same pollutant parameter by any amount;
(2) Technical review criteria (TRC) violations, which are defined as those in which 33 percent or more of wastewater measurements taken for each pollutant parameter during a six-month period equals or exceeds the product of the daily maximum limit or the average limit multiplied by the applicable criteria (1.4 for BOD, TSS, fats, oils and grease, and 1.2 for all other pollutants except pH);
(3) Any other discharge violation that the director believes has caused, alone or in combination with other discharges, interference or pass through, including endangering the health of POTW personnel or the general public;

(7) Failure to accurately report noncompliance; or
(8) Any other violation which the director determines will adversely affect the operation or implementation of the local pretreatment program.
Slug means a discharge at a flow rate or concentration which could cause a violation of the prohibited discharge standards set forth in section 86-133.
Standard industrial classification (SIC) means a classification pursuant to the Standard Industrial Classification Manual issued by the Executive Office of the President, Office of Management and Budget.
Stormwater means a flow that occurs during or following any form of natural precipitation and results from such precipitation, including snow-melt.
Suspended solids mean the total suspended matter that floats on the surface of or is suspended in water, wastewater or other liquids, and which is removable by laboratory filtering.
